"This is bliss! Wide, roomy, foam-soft berths and breakfast
in bed are typical of the luxuries you enjoy on The President
(Pan American's double-decked 'Strato'
Clipper* service).
Burtt and I left New York Friday night at 6 ... arrived in
Rome Saturday in time for a fashionable late dinner."
"At the Vatican, Sunday morning. Burtt snapped me
with one of the Swiss Guards. Costume by Michel-
angelo, he told us! It was thrilling to walk through that
entrance you see behind us. And St. Peter's is magnifi-
cent; the dome, statues and carvings, the intricate
woodwork and solemn grandeur are something you
could never forget! (If you're going to Rome, remember
that Pan American is the only airline that offers 4
routes across the Atlantic—via Glasgow, London, Paris,
Lisbon. You can go one way, return another.)"
On only a week's vacation, Clippers
can give you 7 full days in Italy

From the diary of PAT DUTCHER of Darien, Conn.,
Abroad
who says: "It's a trip we'll never ever forget!"
"Here
you see the
Colosseum,

Charles
Dickens
called 'the ghost of old Rome, wicked, wonderful old city? It's
customary in Rome to stop for a cold drink at a sidewalk cafe
before exploring the spectacular amphitheater.
The courtesy
and speed of Italian waiters are really wonderful!"

"We hired a Cisitalia sports car for one day and
were the envy of every American in Rome. We drove
slowly along the Appian Way.
You can still see the
grooves worn by chariots! We passed stately arches and
temples, ancient aqueducts built by the Caesars."
"I made sure we would return! Throw a coin in
the Trevi fountain, they say, and you're certain to
return to Rome. Burtt and I flew home over Pan
American's sunny southern route via Lisbon."
